learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the necessary knowledge to read and execute mechanical drawings of components, groups and assemblies according to technical drawing standards.

Integrate mechanical drawing skills with notions acquired in metallurgy, machine design, applied mechanics, and mechanical technology courses, fostering awareness of the multidisciplinary nature of engineering with specific references to production systems, technologies, and the design of machinery and mechanical systems.
Acquire the ability to use the appropriate technical language of mechanical drawing.
Summarize and represent the results of design activity using appropriate and updated methods, techniques, and tools to address design and productive issues.
Execute, according to standards, dimensioned sketches of components and simple assemblies.

Read mechanical drawings of components, groups or assemblies, interpreting orthogonal views, dimension indications, dimensional and geometrical tolerance indications, roughness indications, and indications listed in the legend box and bill of components in a correct and comprehensive way.
Communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions to other technical interlocutors, especially graphic information, applying rigorous representation methods.
Learn to execute freehand sketches and develop technical communication skills.

syllabus_topics: The role of the technical drawing in the design/production process

assessment_methods.method: Written test (execution of a mechanical drawing)
Oral test (exposing subjects related to mechanical drawing)

assessment_rules: The level of student learning is assessed through a written test consisting of a mechanical drawing and an oral test on mechanical drawing subjects, both supported on the same date. To pass, students must demonstrate understanding of basic concepts and acquire basic machine design skills. The final mark is the average rating of the written and oral exams, evaluated from 18 to 30 (cum laude). The maximum rating is given for great design abilities in the written test and thorough understanding, methodological rigor, and appropriate technical vocabulary in the oral test.
